candidates.summary: Rhamero West' mother Kelly set up the Meros World Foundation after the 16-year-old was killed

candidates.lead: Rhamero West' mother Kelly set up the Meros World Foundation after the 16-year-old was killed
candidates.evidence_text: 100th bleed kit unveiled after murder of Rhamero West in Old Trafford - BBC News Image caption, Kelly Brown hopes the kits will eventually be as commonplace as defibrillators By Suzanne Hailey and Lynette Horsburgh , North West Published 21 November 2026 The mother of a 16-year-old boy who was stabbed to death and later campaigned to provide bleed-control kits for communities said she was "overwhelmed" as the 100th piece of life-saving equipment was unveiled. Rhamero West was murdered in Old Trafford, Manchester, in September 2021 after a car chase in the city. He had just finished his first day at college. Known as Mero, he was the nephew of former Manchester City and England footballer Shuan Wright-Phillips. Kelly Brown, who set up the MerosWorld Foundation in memory of her son, has campaigned tirelessly for the life-saving kits, which are located across Greater Manchester. She told BBC North West Tonight : "I'm overwhelmed. "I never thought I would be in this position of supplying the 100th cabinet in Greater Manchester but we've got there and it is a big achievement." Image caption, The 100th cabinet was purple rather than the usual red in a tribute to Rhamero's favourite colour The other 99 cabinets holding the bleed kits are red but the 100th example installed at Fallowfield Library is purple - in a tribute to Rhamero's favourite colour. Kelly hopes the kits will eventually be as commonplace as defibrillators. "Both are important. They both save lives," she said. "That's our drive, to get them everywhere." 'Powerful legacy' Kelly said nothing will take away the heartache of losing her son but being able to make a difference - and keep his memory alive - helps. "The pain doesn't go away. I've learnt over time it gets harder," she said. "The charity, and putting up the cabinets, have given me a purpose to help prevent another family going through the pain and heartache that I'm going through right now." Det Sgt Suzie Worth said: "The 100th installation represents a powerful legacy to ensure we do not forget Rhamero and is a testament to the determination of those who have turned personal tragedy into a mission to save lives." Manchester Crown Court heard the teenager was chased through the streets before he was killed. He was found on Norton Street and later died in hospital. Four people have been convicted of Rhamero's murder and subsequently received long jail sentences. candidates.evidence_text: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said Dwayne Fields, the UK's Chief Scout, has called for youth groups to be exempted and said the charity - which sees more than 1.4m overnight stays a year - would be "firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations" The Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government told the BBC that local leaders who introduce the levy "will have the option to exempt certain types of accommodation in their areas, including accommodation which is often used for trips by youth groups like Scouts and Girl They added money raised from the levy will "stay local and be invested in the visitor experience and local growth including in high streets, parks and events" Labour mayors have indicated they would cap the levy at 5% but the legislation contains no maximum limit

candidates.lead: Andrew Kowalczyk had lived in a tower block in Rochdale for 27 years and now calls a bungalow home
candidates.evidence_text: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted' - BBC News Image caption, Andrew Kowalczyk lived on the College Bank estate for 27 years but says he is now happy in his new home By Richard Stead North West Published 21 November 2026 After 27 years living in the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale, Andrew Kowalczyk did not want to leave. But he said he felt the demolition of the flats, which have dominated the town's skyline since the 1960s, was "inevitable" and he was now relieved to have been rehoused. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced last week that the blocks would be bulldozed and replaced with a new College Bank estate of about 600 homes. It comes after a 10-year campaign by residents who wanted the flats to be refurbished and not knocked down but RBH said the demolition was the only "realistic" option. Kowalczyk, 61, who lived in the Mardyke block, said he was reluctant to move out of his "secure" home and the "great views" but he has since been rehomed in a bungalow in Lower Falinge and was now "delighted with it". Residents started to move out of the flats in October last year after long-term safety concerns were raised in October last year. The blocks are almost all empty, with 78 homes out of 766 currently occupied. Some of the remaining tenants have vowed to challenge the demolition decision. But Kowalczyk said: "I didn't want to move from College Bank because you had great views and your home was secure but I knew that - no matter how much we resisted - demolition is bound to happen. "When I looked at my new bungalow in Lower Falinge, it was really clean, there were new tiles, it also had new cupboards, so I made my mind up about moving in really quickly and now I'm delighted with it." Image source, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Image caption, The new College Bank estate is intended to have green spaces between Lower Falinge and the River Roch. Plans for the new £216m College Bank estate include a mix of mid-rise flats and houses, including family homes with three and four bedrooms. Amanda Newton, chief executive of RBH, said: "It will be a really modern, high quality new skyline for Rochdale. "The homes that are on College Bank now would only last for a maximum of 50 years - even if they were refurbished - so what we're doing now is creating homes that will last for almost double that - for the generations of the future". RBH said the new estate would have about 250 extra bed spaces, when compared to the number within the Seven Sisters towers. Image caption, Amanda Newton says the new estate will be a "modern" skyline The housing association said a refurbishment of the blocks would have taken 12 years and cost £269m, plus VAT. Any refurbishment would have been "extremely complex" and involve adding a second staircase, it said. But that is disputed by residents on the College Bank estate, who say any refurbishment would not need to be so expensive. Mark Slater, chair of the Campaign to Save the Seven Sisters, said: "Other 1960s tower blocks have been refurbished and they don't need a second staircase." Image source, Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Image caption, The new College Bank estate would have around 600 homes - including three and four bedroom houses. Ten years ago, about a thousand people lived in the blocks but one of the buildings - Mitchell Hey - is now empty, and only 78 of the flats remain occupied. Salma Ashiq, who has moved from College Bank into a one-bedroom bungalow on the Lower Falinge estate in the last few weeks, said: "I was really anxious about moving because of all the stress, the waiting and the decorating, the building of the new furniture, so the anxiety for me was horrendous." "This new place is great - I had a vision of what I wanted and I think I've got everything," the 47 year-old added. Image caption, Salma Ashiq has moved from College Bank into a bungalow on the Lower Falinge estate. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing first proposed demolishing four of the Seven Sisters tower blocks in 2017 and there followed years of uncertainty. In 2024, Rochdale Council - and the town's MP Paul Waugh - backed calls for the Seven Sisters tower blocks to be protected from demolition. A College Bank Task Force, including RBH, Rochdale Council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority was later set up to examine the options. candidates.evidence_text: Locals who have campaigned to try to save a historical theatre from demolition say they want to buy it after it failed to sell at auction Hulme Hippodrome in Manchester was listed for a reserve price of £895,000, but on Thursday bidding failed to reach that mark The Grade II-listed building was last used for theatre in the 1960s, and has since hosted live recordings of BBC shows, bingo events, and a church congregation. It has been left empty since 2017 Paul Baker, from the Save Hulme Hippodrome campaign group, said they had been "chasing this building for five years" because it represents "working-class culture in this city" so he was "really pleased" it was still available "We thought the price was too high, and so didn't think it was going to get sold," he told BBC Radio Manchester Baker said the group had since decided to investigate whether its members could raise the money needed to bring the theatre into community ownership

candidates.evidence_text: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme, which supports aspiring lawyers from under-represented backgrounds, had given her the confidence to "reach my goals" and "opened doors" The bursary is a tribute to 18-year-old Anthony, who had ambitions to study law but was murdered in a racist attack on Merseyside in 2005 Uche said she had been inspired by his family's fight for justice and wanted to draw on Anthony's own values when building her career Anthony's mother, Dr Gee Walker, set up a foundation in her son's name to tackle racism, hate crime and discrimination In partnership with the CPS and the National Black Crown Prosecution Association, the foundation offers an Anthony Walker Bursary - as well as a mentor - to help aspiring lawyers from under-represented Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds in the north-west of England

candidates.evidence_text: British television, theatre and film star Helen Fraser, who was perhaps best known for her role in the hit prison drama Bad Girls, has died The actress, who also appeared in episodes of Coronation Street and The Royle Family, reportedly died on 10 November at Yaxley House Care Home, in Eye, Suffolk. She was 84 Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter Handford From 2004 until 2019, she was also an ambassador for East Anglia's Children's Hospices (EACH). The charity said it was "deeply saddened" by her death and would "remember her with enormous fondness and gratitude" "Helen was very special to us and a wonderful ambassador, supporter and friend who worked tirelessly to champion our cause," a spokesperson said "Whether fundraising, attending events, opening our shops or rallying our volunteers, Helen brought incredible warmth, empathy and joy

candidates.evidence_text: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said Dwayne Fields, the UK's Chief Scout, has called for youth groups to be exempted and said the charity - which sees more than 1.4m overnight stays a year - would be "firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations" The Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government told the BBC that local leaders who introduce the levy "will have the option to exempt certain types of accommodation in their areas, including accommodation which is often used for trips by youth groups like Scouts and Girl They added money raised from the levy will "stay local and be invested in the visitor experience and local growth including in high streets, parks and events" Labour mayors have indicated they would cap the levy at 5% but the legislation contains no maximum limit

candidates.evidence_text: Locals who have campaigned to try to save a historical theatre from demolition say they want to buy it after it failed to sell at auction Hulme Hippodrome in Manchester was listed for a reserve price of £895,000, but on Thursday bidding failed to reach that mark The Grade II-listed building was last used for theatre in the 1960s, and has since hosted live recordings of BBC shows, bingo events, and a church congregation. It has been left empty since 2017 Paul Baker, from the Save Hulme Hippodrome campaign group, said they had been "chasing this building for five years" because it represents "working-class culture in this city" so he was "really pleased" it was still available "We thought the price was too high, and so didn't think it was going to get sold," he told BBC Radio Manchester Baker said the group had since decided to investigate whether its members could raise the money needed to bring the theatre into community ownership

The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on An investigation by the Manchester Evening News has revealed that the council failed to publish mandatory transparency records for staff procureme Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:33, 22 Nov 2026 An investigation has revealed a Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on by council staff Some councils across the country use government procurement cards , sometimes referred to as p-cards, for low-value and ad-hoc purchases. They have been described as 'essentially a company credit card' used by eligible council staff They can be used to make emergency payments, reduce paperwork, and speed up purchases from suppliers. However under local government transparency rules introduced in 2015, councils across the country who use them are required to publish what payments have been made to reassure pe Oldham council have now admitted they have not been revealing how these cards were being used and what taxpayer money has been spent on for eleven years. This is after no public records for payments were found by the Manchester Evening News The council is now working on publishing seven years' worth of payment records, which is understood to be the length of time this data is required to be kept. Over this period, over £1m was spent by council and school staff

candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham Potential Altrincham Grammar School for Girls admissions policy change sparks concern Some think the change is unfair Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:58, 21 Nov 2026 Altrincham Grammar School for Girls (Image: Ma A proposal to change the admission policy at a Trafford grammar school has prompted concerns it could disadvantage local girls AGGS has four feeder schools - Acre Hall Primary School, in Urmston ; Barton Clough Primary School, in Stretford ; Elmridge Primary School, in Hale Barns; and Lime Tree Primary Academy, in Sale Concerns have been raised that girls could miss out on a place simply because they have not attended the right primary school. Those speaking against the move have pointed out this could include those living and studying in Altrincham itself, as well as nearby areas such as Broad Looked-after children, and those living in the catchment area who receive a ‘pupil premium’ or who have a sister already at the school still make up the top three priority categories under the proposed change If space remains after feeder school pupils are then taken into account, places will then be given to those in the catchment area with those living closest offered places first

english_fact_card.what_happened: The next stage of home-building at the Rivington Chase development in Horwich will involve moving 250,000 tonnes of spoil across the site. Bellway said building 345 new homes at the site of the former Horwich Loco works would mean creating a haul road to shift materials from the building area to an open space area elsewhere within the development.
english_fact_card.when: Planning was recently granted by Bolton council for phases four and five of the massive development, which will eventually see more than 900 homes built at the 150 acre regeneration site.
english_fact_card.who_affected: Residents and road users in Horwich and surrounding areas, as the promised link road connecting Chorley New Road with Middlebrook remains incomplete due to a land dispute.
english_fact_card.why_now: The project has been hit by a promised link road connecting Chorley New Road with Middlebrook, originally slated for completion in 2021 and later targeted for spring 2025 being delayed. The £19 million road is still incomplete due to a land dispute remaining unresolved.
english_fact_card.reader_value: Local residents and commuters should be aware of ongoing construction activity and the continued delay of the link road, which was intended to relieve congestion.
english_fact_card.reader_action: Monitor Bolton council updates on the link road completion and be prepared for construction traffic in the Horwich area.

candidates.english_reader_card: Bolton council has granted planning for phases four and five of the Rivington Chase development in Horwich, involving 345 new homes and the movement of 250,000 tonnes of spoil. The fire broke out inside a room at the DoubleTree by Hilton hotel, on Auburn Street near Manchester Piccadilly railway station, early on Saturday morning (November 21) One guest involved estimated some 500 people were ordered outside as the fire service attended The fire is understood to have broken out in a room on the fourth floor. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Doctor jailed for sexually abusing patients makes shameless bid for freedom Dr Wayne Sefton denied all wrongdoing, but was found guilty of indecent assault and assault by penetration Wayne Davis (Image: Manchester Evening News) Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 07:23, 21 Nov 2026 Updated 10:27, 21 Nov 2026 Judges have rejected an appeal bid against the conviction of a doctor who sexually abused his female patients. Dr Wayne Sefton Davis, of Salford , was jailed in January 2025 for The 69-year-old was unanimously found guilty at his trial in December 2024, of sexually abusing the patients over a 15-year period whilst he worked as a general practitioner He denied all wrongdoing, but was found guilty of indecent assault and assault by penetration. Davis was jailed for eight years in January 2025 and ordered to sign the sex offender register for life It came after he conducted unnecessary, intimate examinations on two female patients between 1995 and 2006. He told one of his victims, a member of the Chassidic orthodox Jewish community, that he was going to 'stretch' her after she went to see him because she was finding sex pa "She felt traumatised by what happened. She knew what happened felt wrong and bad," prosecutor Vanessa Thomson told the court. Worried about speaking out against such a highly-regarded man, the victim didn't report the matter to police until years later

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Scouts fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price kids out of camping trips A Manchester Scout leader dubbed the levy the 'tent tax' Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and David Hughes Press Association Polit Scout groups fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price some kids out of camping trips. The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Cops at 'breaking point' as GMP struggles to secure Andy Burnham's No 10 North Exclusive: Police rest days are routinely cancelled as part of Operation Ember, it is said Andy Burnham at No 10 North (Image: Oli Scarff - WPA Pool/Getty Imag Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 06:34, 22 Nov 2026 Officers at Greater Manchester Police tasked with ensuring the security of Andy Burnham when he visits his home and No 10 North are at 'breaking point' Exhausted cops are routinely being ordered to cancel rest days to patrol the prime minister's office at Heron House in Manchester city centre and his home when he heads north, according to Sgt Mike Peake, chair of the Greater Manchester branch of the Police Federation, the cops’ GMP's stretched resources are being augmented by 'mutual aid', help from forces around the country who are sending officers to Manchester to bolster the ranks, other sources have told the Manchester Evening News . They are being put up in hotels and adding to a predicted £10m ove They also claim the PM's office regularly gives GMP very late notice of the movements of the PM. It is suggested his diary is often revealed on a Monday for that Monday and the rest of the week, frequently giving bosses at GMP just hours to ensure the right resources are on hand One of Mr Burnham's first acts as PM was to set up No 10 North as part of an effort to decentralise power and decision-making which has previously always been at Whitehall in London. It prompted a huge security operation by GMP, dubbed Operation Ember

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on An investigation by the Manchester Evening News has revealed that the council failed to publish mandatory transparency records for staff procureme Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:33, 22 Nov 2026 An investigation has revealed a Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on by council staff Some councils across the country use government procurement cards , sometimes referred to as p-cards, for low-value and ad-hoc purchases. They have been described as 'essentially a company credit card' used by eligible council staff They can be used to make emergency payments, reduce paperwork, and speed up purchases from suppliers. However under local government transparency rules introduced in 2015, councils across the country who use them are required to publish what payments have been made to reassure pe Oldham council have now admitted they have not been revealing how these cards were being used and what taxpayer money has been spent on for eleven years. This is after no public records for payments were found by the Manchester Evening News The council is now working on publishing seven years' worth of payment records, which is understood to be the length of time this data is required to be kept. Over this period, over £1m was spent by council and school staff

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Scouts fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price kids out of camping trips A Manchester Scout leader dubbed the levy the 'tent tax' Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and David Hughes Press Association Polit Scout groups fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price some kids out of camping trips. The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale grooming scandal Rochdale grooming gang leader victim fears he's living near her 'Angelina' has told how she wants to move 200 miles away Add to preferred sources News Paul Britton Reporter 09:44, 21 Nov 2026 Shabir Ahmed (Image: GMP) A victim of Rochdale grooming gang ringleader Shabir Ahmed has told how she fears he's now living near her - and how she's preparing to move more than 200 miles away as a result Ahmed - known by his victims as 'Daddy' - was sentenced to 19 years in prison at Liverpool Crown Court in 2012 as one of nine men convicted of offences against five girls. He was released in July after serving 14 years In a situation that has caused a diplomatic row, the 73-year-old can't be deported because of a 1971 law applying to Commonwealth citizens who arrived in the UK more than 50 years ago. It is being called a 'loophole' Ahmed has been stripped of his British citizenship, leaving him solely as a Pakistani national Following his release, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said her intention was to change the legal loophole to make it possible to deport those convicted of serious crimes , including terrorism and child sexual exploitation. Pakistan has insisted it will not accept Ahmed's return

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham Huge cordon in place as man in his 70s 'seriously hurt' in Altrincham According to eyewitnesses, an air ambulance landed at the scene Add to preferred sources Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 16:02, 20 Nov 2026 Th A pensioner has been rushed to hospital with 'serious' injuries after being hit by a car in Altrincham . The crash happened on near the junction of Stamford New Road and Moss Lane in Altrincham town centre at around 1pm on Friday (November 20) Police and paramedics were called to the scene and road closures were put in place as crews responded. Reports on social media suggest an air ambulance also landed and later took off from the Oakfield Road car park A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Police said the man, aged in his 70s, was taken to hospital from the scene with 'serious injuries'. No arrests were made and the road closures have since been lifted Junction of Stamford New Road and Moss Lane in Altrincham (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News) A spokesperson for the force said: "We were called shortly before 1pm to reports of an RTC involving a car vs pedestrian

His health had significantly deteriorated in the years prior to his death. He had become immobile and bed bound prior to his death due to his profound neurological disability Examination of his brain following his death confirmed an in life diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease In addition, he was found to have high stage chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), stage 3 Limbic-predominant age related TPD-43 encephalopathy (LATE) and small vessel cerebrovascular disease. candidates.evidence_text: The actress, who also appeared in episodes of Coronation Street and The Royle Family, reportedly died on 10 November at Yaxley House Care Home, in Eye, Suffolk. She was 84 Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter Handford From 2004 until 2019, she was also an ambassador for East Anglia's Children's Hospices (EACH). The charity said it was "deeply saddened" by her death and would "remember her with enormous fondness and gratitude" "Helen was very special to us and a wonderful ambassador, supporter and friend who worked tirelessly to champion our cause," a spokesperson said "Whether fundraising, attending events, opening our shops or rallying our volunteers, Helen brought incredible warmth, empathy and joy "She had a wonderful way with people and made a lasting impression on all those fortunate enough to spend time in her company."

candidates.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

evidence_packet.summary: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Children and families are set to benefit from improved play areas in Failsworth after Oldham Council secured £270,000 from the Government's Playground Fund The funding forms part of an £18million government programme to create or refurbish playgrounds in England's areas of greatest need over the next two years The government selected Failsworth to receive a share of the fund, with three play areas identified as eligible for investment through the programme for 66 local authorities Funding will be used to improve playground facilities and support community-led design and engagement activities, giving residents the opportunity to help shape the future of these spaces The three eligible sites are Higher Memorial Park which will receive £160,000, Daisy Nook Country Park which will receive £60,000 and Lower Memorial Park which has been allocated £50,000 A larger share will go to Higher Memorial Park because this has received significantly less external investment than the other locations in recent years

candidates.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026 The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications Residents will be asked the following question “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton’s providing new forms of support for residents struggling with the cost of living, as presented at Bolton’s Tackling Poverty networking event held at Bolton Albert Halls on November 12 The cost of living is a major concern for many, and it may get tougher during the winter, as such, the event and the targeted support offered to people across Bolton offer some reassurance to those worst affected The support spans a large number of areas including helping access emergency food, heating, and financial assistance The event brings those organisations providing support together so they can better understand what is available across the town and as such can make informed decisions about who to refer people to for the most appropriate help In total there were over 40 organisations attending the event including the public, voluntary, and community sector, and other parters who were highlighting their services all were encouraged to network, share information, and create a more connected and efficient framework The presentations highlighted how Bolton’s Tacking Poverty Strategy can make a real difference, and how the Crisis, and Resilience Fund is being allocated to help groups across the borough

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Jo Platt MP with GM Blood Bikes Chair Russ Harrison, Leader of Wigan Council Cllr Nazia Rehman, and Wigan Council representatives Wigan Council has become one of the first local authorities in Greater Manchester to formally allow Blood Bikes to use bus lanes while carrying out their vital duties The council has amended its bus lane Traffic Regulation Order (TRO) to allow Blood Bike riders on official duties to legally use bus lanes across the borough, helping to ease the journey of volunteers and reduce the risk of unnecessary delays A volunteer-led charity, Greater Manchester Blood Bikes transport blood, plasma, vaccines, breast milk, emergency medicine and more to hospitals and healthcare settings all year round Leader of Wigan Council, Councillor Nazia Rehman, said: “I am incredibly proud that we are leading the way to give Blood Bikes riders access to bus lanes while carrying out their vital duties “These volunteers provide an invaluable service to our communities and NHS, and this decision is a practical way of recognising their dedication and commitment

Through a process of reflection and catharsis the sculptures were created in carefully devised, movement informed workshops with individuals who have experience of grief. Made using tr The central space is immersed in sanguine red. Suspended moulded set plaster works produced with membrane-like hessian, appear as husks, shells, figures metamorphosed into an upturned archaeological dig; an enigmatic psychological landscape that defies the laws of physics; or cyc The duality between absence and upsurge is continued in Peake’s chalk works on paper. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

Cadno Lounge, Neath . Loungers, the West Country‑based café‑bar group, will open Fosforo Lounge, King Street in Stretford on Saturday 28th November 2026, creating around 30 new jobs for local people.. . Fosforo Lounge will be open all day, every day, serving breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner and drinks, with dedicated kids’, gluten‑free and vegan menus. . The site on King Street has been transformed by the Loungers design team into a warm, eclectic ‘home from home’ – their signature style. Fosforo translates to matchstick and is a nod to Manchester-based painter LS Lowry’s ‘matchstick men’ style.. . Fosforo Lounge’s all‑day menu will cater for every taste, from hearty comfort food to healthier choices and indulgent treats. Families are a major focus, with games, books, colouring materials, high chairs and baby‑changing facilities available for Little Loungers.. . With community at its heart, Fosforo Lounge will offer a welcoming space for regular meet‑ups, business catch‑ups, book clubs, knitting groups, parent‑and‑baby sessions, creative workshops and more. Local groups looking for a friendly, flexible venue will be encouraged to get in touch.. . Vix Connolly, General Manager, Fosforo Lounge said: “We’re so looking forward to welcoming everyone to Fosforo Lounge on the 28th November. Becoming a genuine part of the community is incredibly important to us, and we can’t wait to meet our neighbours and get involved locally.. . “If you’re looking for a friendly, flexible space for events or group meet‑ups, pop in once we’re open – we’d love to chat and see how we can help.”. . . . . . . All of the independent traders showcasing here produce high quality, handmade, artisan goods. The Makers Market pride themselves on having a wide range of truly unique stallholders, offering delicious treats, amazing art and craft and so much more. Whether you’re looking for an ideal gift, a treat for yourself, or just topping up your weekly shopping, this market is a great place to spend time at the weekend. Taking place on the Piazza of Media City Outlet Mall outside the famous Lowry Theatre, Salford, Manchester, Quayside Media City Makers Market provides plenty of fun, entertainment, and unique shopping opportunities in the heart of the city. Set by the stunning waterside, which is surrounded by the BBC and ITV studios, it’s a buzzing event with a mix of local makers, foodies and family fun in a modern, iconic setting. Taking place usually on the last Saturday and Sunday of the month, there’s additional dates on Bank Holidays and at Christmas so plenty of chances to catch this market. candidates.evidence_text: Clint Boon spinning records on Greek Street on a Saturday afternoon, and it won’t cost you a penny. Stopford Park is throwing a free party to launch Bosden, the first of its new apartment buildings, just up from the Town Hall Clint Boon needs very little introduction round these parts. The Inspiral Carpets man was right in the middle of Madchester and he’s still at it, touring and recently publishing his book, The Manchester Chronicles . He’ll be sharing the decks with DJ, presenter and podcaster Matt There’ll be a talk from John Barratt, co-founder of the Stockport Music Story with his wife Rosemary. John founded the record label Facsimile Liaisons which took him to Strawberry Studios, he’s worked with Easterhouse and Syncopation, and also signed The Family Foundation, Ultrac There will be a pop-up from I Knead Pizza, and it’s also the first chance to have a nosey round the show apartment at Bosden with the remaining apartments going on the market the same day. If you’re tempted to have a look round you can register your interest here Make a weekend of it: Foodie Friday is on across the Market Place and Great Underbank the night before, from 6pm

candidates.evidence_text: English National Opera and Factory International bring Philip Glass and Robert Wilson’s revolutionary opera Einstein on the Beach to Aviva Studios in 2027 Inspired by Albert Einstein ’ theories on space, time and quantum physics, which changed how we see the universe, this 50th anniversary production will reimagine the iconic work through ‘once-in-a-lifetime experiential staging.’ Combining music, theatre, live art and light, sculpture and movement, the upcoming iteration of Einstein on the Beach invites audiences into a 360-degree world where Einstein’s ideas and Glass’s music are felt all around. Vast in scale, the production features a huge cast of voca The show provides Phelim McDermott, acclaimed director and co-founder of Improbable, with the opportunity to complete the Glass Portrait Trilogy . Having directed Satyagraha in 2026 and the Grammy and Olivier Award-winning production of Akhnaten in 2016 for English National Opera The star-studded lineup also sees the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, led by acclaimed conductor and composer Brad Lubman, return to the venue following their collaboration with ENO and Factory International on the genre-defying opera, Angel’s Bone . Meanwhile, a 16-strong vocal ense Einstein on the Beach will run in Philip Glass’s 90th year, opening at Aviva Studios from Sat 29 May 2027 – Sat 12 June 2027, followed by its North American premiere at the Park Avenue Armory, New York

It blends village charm with urban convenience and a vibrant community atmosphere. It boasts gorgeous historic buildings alongside a whole network of trendy, independent hospitality and retail businesses. And it Hidden beneath the surface of all this are stories. Lots and lots of stories. From screen-worthy romances to notorious murderers via whole potato-swallowers and eccentric aldermen, Didsbury has the lot. From years spent languishing in post-industrial decline to being crowned one of ‘the coolest neighbourhoods in the world’ in the blink of an eye. What’s the story here? Find out with Jonathan Schofield Tours, with whom you’ll track Ancoats’ changes by strolling its streets, crossing its canals, and taking a look inside one of its most fascinating buildings Starting at Cutting Room Square, your expert tour guide will reveal the layers of history that make Ancoats special, from its place in establishing Manchester’s reputation as ‘Cottonopolis’ to the notorious street gangs, or ‘scuttlers’, who once patrolled and fought here But this winsome stroll is also about the urban regeneration and cultural energy of Ancoats today, which boasts everything from grassroots theatres to Manchester’s only Michelin-starred restaurant

This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

Anna Clough, a Cumbrian-born artist based at Salford’s Paradise Works, has made walking performances tracing mining landscapes from the Neo Sheffield’s Charlotte Dawson treats everyday objects – souvenirs, collections – as vessels for memory. candidates.evidence_text: Football Mauricio Pochettino Mauricio Pochettino's Liverpool preparation 'not ideal' as Man United boss learns size of job Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of Manchester United for the first time against Liverpool on Sunday having only arrived in England on Wednesday Ad Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is gearing up for his first game at the helm against Liverpool . But former Premier League striker Duncan Ferguson thinks the Argentine's pre-match preparation has not been ideal United's hierarchy acted swiftly after Michael Carrick's tenure became untenable last week. After one win in 10 Premier League games, the manager was sacked, and new head coach Pochettino was poached from the USMNT It has been a hectic few days for the former Spurs and Chelsea boss. He was flown in via private jet in the early hours of Wednesday after overseeing one last game for the US against Haiti on Tuesday. He then took training on Thursday, which was subject to controversy after part That session will be one of only three Pochettino can oversee with his new players before he heads to Anfield on Sunday. Ex-Everton man Ferguson thinks that this prep is far from ideal when facing a bitter rival in a huge televised clash Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!

Moyes: ‘I want Jack to show more’ David Moyes has said he wants Jack Grealish to produce more for Everton as he prepares to reintegrate the playmaker into the squad Grealish has missed Everton’s past four games mainly for disciplinary reasons having failed to report for training before last month’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. His last appearance for the team was in the 2-0 loss to Chelsea on 17 October but he is fit and available for Mon “He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before,” the Everton manager said. “We will get on with things. The team is doing really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.” The 31-year-old played in a behind-closed-doors fixture against Derby last week andalso apologised on social media for being unable to help the team, who won three of four matches in his absence. Grealish, however, had struggled to replicate last season’s form impact when joining He added: “Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, more goals. There’s lots of things about him which we need and he’s good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope The Everton manager has backed Jordan Pickford to respond strongly to the threat from James Trafford to his England place, following after the Leeds goalkeeper’s inclusion and impressive display in the Nations League win over Spain

После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он прио 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне!
